title: Learn JavaScript from the ground up
hook: JavaScript is the language of the web and Node.js. This track starts with plain English and small examples, then grows into the event loop, closures, async, memory, and the depth you need for senior interviews.

blocks.text: JavaScript is a dynamically typed language standardized as ECMAScript. You write .js or .mjs files. An engine like V8 parses source, compiles hot functions with Just-In-Time (JIT) optimization, and runs your code on a single thread coordinated by the event loop. The host (browser or Node.js) supplies APIs for DOM, fetch, fs, and timers — they are not the language itself.

entries.plainDefinition: The official specification JavaScript implements. ES2015 (ES6) and later versions add classes, modules, async/await, and more.
entries.example: const and arrow functions come from ES2015.

entries.plainDefinition: Google's JavaScript engine used in Chrome and Node.js. Parses, compiles, and runs JS with JIT optimization.
entries.example: Node.js runs your server code inside V8.

entries.plainDefinition: The scheduler that runs JavaScript on one thread, draining the call stack then microtasks then macrotasks.
entries.example: Promise.then callbacks are microtasks; setTimeout is a macrotask.

diagram.title: How JavaScript runs
diagram.source:
flowchart LR

  D --> E[Event loop]
  E --> F[Your program runs]

sections.heading: How it differs from C# and TypeScript

blocks.text: If you know C# or TypeScript, JavaScript feels familiar in syntax but different at run time. Types are checked at run time through coercion, not at compile time. Privacy is convention (# private fields help). async/await sits on Promises and the event loop, not CLR Tasks on thread-pool threads.

blocks.title: JavaScript vs C# and TypeScript
rows: Compile time (TS) or compile + run time (C#)
C#: thread pool; TS: same as JS
C#: nominal classes; TS: structural interfaces
C#: access modifiers enforced by CLR

blocks.text: Modules are numbered in learning order. Work through them in sequence unless a time map below fits your schedule. Each module ends with a mind map, a one-screen quick overview, and an interview page. This track has 18 modules and 110 topics.

items.title: Foundations (modules 01–07)
items.body: Runtime, syntax, types/coercion, functions/closures, objects/prototypes, errors, and null safety. Finish before async or memory modules.

items.title: Intermediate (modules 08–13)
items.body: Collections, structural patterns, callbacks/events, modern syntax, functional methods, and Promises/async/event loop.

items.title: Advanced (modules 14–18)
items.body: Memory/GC, Workers, modules/tooling, browser vs Node, and ES recap with interview radar.

items.title: Revise with mind maps and interview pages
items.body: Use mind maps and interview sections to reinforce what you learned — not as a shortcut around the topic pages.

items.title: Senior / FAANG depth layer (5+ years)
items.body: On intermediate and advanced topics (08–18), read the Senior interview depth section after the beginner steps. Priority: microtasks-vs-macrotasks, closures-and-capture, implementing-promise-from-scratch, v8-garbage-collection, debounce-throttle-implementations.

blocks.title: 110 topics — beginner clarity plus senior depth
blocks.body: Every topic keeps plain-English hooks and glossaries. Intermediate and advanced modules add runtime internals, tradeoffs, and FAANG-style interview scripts without removing the beginner layer.

stages.title: Foundations (01–07)
stages.summary: Learn what happens from source text to running code in V8 and other engines. Covers parsing, execution contexts, the call stack, hoisting, strict mode, and how JavaScript differs from C# on the CLR.

stages.title: Intermediate (08–13)
stages.summary: Array, Map, Set, WeakMap, WeakSet, typed arrays, iterators, generators, yield, and performance tradeoffs for cache keys and large datasets.

stages.title: Advanced (14–18)
stages.summary: Stack versus heap, object headers, GC generations, closure retention, memory leaks, WeakRef, FinalizationRegistry, and V8 versus CLR GC.

timeMaps.focus: Skim foundations. Focus on runtime/types and the topic that maps to your weakest interview area.
Complete modules 01–13 with interview pages. Leave 14–18 for a third sitting.
All 18 modules in order. Use mind maps and interview pages as revision.
Deep-read Senior interview depth on modules 08–18. Priority: event loop, closures, Promises, memory/GC, debounce/throttle implementations.
